newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine banks to register non-resident Tbill deals.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine banks to register non-resident Tbill deals.

text.p: Ukrainian commercial banks must register all Treasury bill deals by non-residents at the central bank within three days after the deal is signed, starting from February 25, and register all existing deals by that date, the central bank said on Thursday.

"In future deals made by commercial banks with non-residents Treasury bill market operations, copies of the agreements must be presented to the National Bank of Ukraine within three days after they are signed," the central bank said in an instruction sent by electronic mail to banks and obtained by Reuters.
"Commercial banks do not have the right to serve clients on the T-bill market without registering the deal at the central bank," the central bank statement added.
The instruction said the central bank would assign each client a code, and the client would not have the right to undertake T-bill purchases using any other code.
One official who asked not to be named said the new rule was designed to give the central bank an overview of who was active in the lucrative market.
"It's senseless. There is such a thing as secrecy. Foreigners want to participate in the market, and it's no good for Ukraine either. It will just make dealers' jobs harder," one Western banker said.
The banker said the rule sounded like an attempt to limit foreign participation in the market.
But Western bankers and economists said earlier that Ukraine had quietly shelved plans to impose specific limits on foreign T-bill buying as the Justice Ministry had rejected it.
Central Bank chief Viktor Yushchenko and Deputy Finance Minister Andry Lytvyn have said they were proposing to curb foreign participation, estimated at 80 percent of activity.

The relative stability of the new hryvnia currency, at 1.8050 to the dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Wednesday after 1.8500 on Monday, and slowing inflation have made the market attractive to foreigners.
Ukrainian dealers said non-resident buying on the T-bill market was pushing upthe hryvnia.
